hero_image.prompt: Premium robotics textbook illustration of a small wheeled educational rover named RoboRover on a clean graph-paper floor map, showing its planar pose with x and y world axes, a heading arrow, a curved trajectory, and a subtle distinction between a fixed world frame and a body frame attached to the rover. Technically plausible two-wheel rover, restrained modern engineering style, clear lighting, no decorative sci-fi elements, minimal essential labels only.
hero_image.caption: RoboRover's pose describes where it is and which way it is facing, while its velocity describes how that pose is changing.
hero_image.alt_text: A small wheeled rover on a coordinate grid with a curved path, world axes, and a heading arrow illustrating position, orientation, and motion.

inline_visuals.prompt: Educational technical diagram showing a top-down wheeled rover at position x,y on a fixed world coordinate grid. Draw a world x-axis and y-axis, a robot body frame with forward and left axes attached to the rover, a heading angle theta between the world x-axis and robot forward direction, and a short curved path arrow. Use precise geometry, restrained textbook colors, clean linework, and only essential labels.
inline_visuals.caption: The world frame stays fixed, while the body frame rotates with RoboRover.
inline_visuals.alt_text: Top-down coordinate diagram of a rover showing fixed world axes, robot-attached body axes, heading angle theta, and a curved direction of travel.

inline_visuals.prompt: Technically accurate top-down engineering illustration of RoboRover starting at x=1 m, y=2 m, facing east, moving forward at constant 0.50 m/s while rotating counterclockwise at 0.20 rad/s for 3 seconds. Show the circular arc, start and final pose, radius labeled 2.50 m, final heading angle about 0.60 rad, and a separate curved path-length annotation. Use a clean coordinate grid and restrained publication-quality colors; labels must be sparse and legible.
inline_visuals.caption: A constant forward speed combined with a constant turn rate produces a circular arc, not a straight path.
inline_visuals.alt_text: Top-down diagram of a rover following a counterclockwise circular arc from an initial pose to a final pose, with turning radius and heading change indicated.

inline_visuals.prompt: Premium engineering cutaway-style illustration comparing an ideal kinematic prediction with a real small wheeled rover on a floor. Show the predicted smooth trajectory as a thin dashed line and the actual slipping or slightly miscalibrated trajectory as a nearby solid line, with subtle callouts for wheel slip, unequal wheel calibration, command latency, and pose error. Keep the robot physically plausible, avoid hazardous hardware, use a clean robotics textbook layout, and do not make the image text-heavy.
inline_visuals.caption: Kinematics predicts an ideal motion; slip, calibration, latency, and mechanical limits can make the real path different.
inline_visuals.alt_text: A wheeled rover with two nearby trajectories, one ideal and one deviating due to wheel slip and calibration errors.
